messages:
megan: FYI got an escalated ticket — customer reports large latency regressions on /v1/toolcall when using function-calling + JSON schema validation. p95 jumped ~300ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~2.8s. Happened around 2024-04-15 09:02 UTC. Trace id: trace-8f7b3c. :warning:

ashwin: thanks — any repro steps from the customer? request size, model, schema? :eyes:

megan: customer says they call our tool router with function-calling, large nested schema (~15 fields, arrays). sample payload they shared:
```json
{
  "model": "rwd-1-large",
  "input": "Summarize...",
  "tools": ["search", "db_write"],
  "schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"},"attrs":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}}}}}}
```

jordan: logs/trace look like validation CPU spikes inside the tool-router process. I see repeated JSONSchema.validate calls in the hot path. snippet from router logs:
```
2024-04-15T09:02:12Z tool-router INFO id=trace-8f7b3c step=handle_request latency=45ms
2024-04-15T09:02:12Z tool-router INFO id=trace-8f7b3c step=validate_schema latency=1840ms
2024-04-15T09:02:12Z tool-router INFO id=trace-8f7b3c step=invoke_tool latency=800ms
```

lucy: confirmed on infra side — tool-router pod CPU climbs to 95% for these requests, backlog forms, batching delays increase overall latency. Flamegraph attached in internal thread (link). Looks regression-y vs last-week baseline where validate_schema was ~120ms.

ashwin: possible causes: heavier schema + nested arrays triggering exponential validation cost; also we recently landed stricter full-schema validation (allOf / patternProperties) in PR #4123 — could be combinatorial explosion for some patterns.

megan: customer needs short-term mitigation while we root cause. They want either lower latency or a config to bypass heavy validation.

jordan: short-term mitigation ideas:
- add per-request schema validation timeout (fail-to-permissive)
- add a feature-flag to bypass schema validation for large schemas (>10k chars or >N nodes)
- route function-calls to a "no-validation" worker pool for latency-sensitive customers
- increase router concurrency / add autoscale policy for router when validation latency spikes

lucy: ops note: increasing worker count helps but increases cost and may only mask worst-case CPU contention. I can spin up an additional replica pool for the affected tenant while we deploy a proper fix.

megan: customer prefers a config flag. can we toggle permissive mode on their account quickly?

ashwin: yes — we have a hidden account-level flag: tool.router.schema_validation=full|permissive|off. I can flip to permissive (still checks shape, skips deep keyword checks) for acct-123. Requires a small config change + quick rollout. Will do canary for 5% traffic first. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout start: vault://config/acct-123/tool.router.schema_validation -> permissive (canary=5%) by ashwin at 2024-04-15T09:37:10Z

lucy: after canary metrics (10m): p95 for acct-123 dropped to 420ms (was 1.2s), p99 to 650ms (was 2.8s). CPU now stable ~40-55%.

megan: replied to customer with mitigation and timeline. they accepted permissive mode as temporary. :white_check_mark:

jordan: long-term actions:
- optimize schema validator (cache compiled validators per schema hash, use Ajv-like compiled functions)
- add a fast-path for common patterns (simple arrays/objects no regex/allOf)
- telemetry: emit schema complexity metric so we can detect/auto-bail for heavy schemas
- consider moving validation out of hot request path (async validate + annotate) for non-blocking routes

ashwin: I'll open an RFC and a ticket to replace sync validator with compiled validators and schema hash cache. Also will add the account-level flag to console with docs.

megan: created support follow-up checklist and informed customer of RFC timeline. Closing the support escalations thread unless anyone needs more on-call help.

lucy: leaving a note to revisit autoscale thresholds for tool-router in SLO playbook.

megan: thanks all. filing the internal postmortem in #postmortems with mitigation timeline and customer comms. :pray:
